name: Symbols that moved most
brief:
An end-of-day report lists the symbols whose price moved most. Trade `i` was in `syms[i]` at `px[i]`, in time order. For each symbol take its first and last price; its move is the size of the change, last less first, divided by the first price. A symbol is a mover when its move is at least `pct` per cent, tested exactly as `std::abs(last - first) * 100 >= pct * first`. Write `movers(syms, px, pct)`, which returns the movers, largest move first, and symbols with equal moves in alphabetical order.

For trades `VOD 100, BARC 250, VOD 104, AZN 5000, BARC 240, AZN 5050` and `pct = 2`, VOD and BARC both moved 4% and AZN 1%. The answer is `{"BARC", "VOD"}`.
constraints: $0 \le n \le 10^5$ trades, every price above 0. A symbol traded once has a move of 0.
Equal moves in the tests are exactly equal, so compare them directly.
hint: A `std::map` from symbol to its first and last price keeps one entry per symbol. Record the first price only when the symbol is new.

examples.note: VOD 4/100 and BARC 10/250 tie at 4%; AZN moved 1%.

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: `seen.find` before `emplace` keeps the first price; `seen[sym] = ...` on every trade would overwrite it.
The move is measured against the first price, so a fall from 100 to 80 is 20%, not 25%.
The sort key is the move, then the symbol, which gives one fixed order whatever order the map holds.

planted.slip: Measures the move against the last price instead of the first.
A move of exactly pct per cent is left out.
Writes the first price on every trade, so first and last are always equal.
